newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Diplomats alarmed by Croat use of fascist slogans.
newsitem.headline: Diplomats alarmed by Croat use of fascist slogans.

text.p: Western diplomats said on Thursday they were deeply concerned over the use of fascist slogans by Bosnian Croat authorities in medal ceremonies this month.
Speaking at a ceremony this week in the southern town of Mostar, a Bosnian Croat police officer employed a fascist slogan associated with Croatia's Nazi puppet regime during World War Two.
"God and Croats, prepare for home!" officer Zlatan Mijo Jelic told special policemen after awarding them medals from Croatian President Franjo Tudjman.
Croat officials used the same slogan in another medal ceremony for Bosnian Croat militia earlier this month, Croat media reported.
Western envoys said the ceremonies indicated that Bosnian Croat authorities felt they could pursue hardline nationalist policies with impunity.
"There's a lot of rewriting of history going on here," said one official based in Mostar, who asked not to be named.
The International High Representative to Bosnia, Carl Bildt, said he had called on diplomats from major powers to discuss a diplomatic response.
"I think the international community must be very vigilant on these cases," Bildt told Reuters late on Wednesday.

Bildt, who oversees the implementation of a Bosnian peace treaty, said that major powers could not tolerate attempts to glorify the Nazi "Ustasha" state that massacred Jews and Serbs during World War Two.
"These are sensitive issues because there is a Croat past, if we go back to the Ustasha period, which is still living in the memories of people living here.
"If we are not honest and open and clear in dealing with that past, the ugly past of this region, then I think we lose credibility in dealing with the problems of the present."
Bildt also said Bosnian Croats were still using symbols from the self-styled state of Herzeg-Bosna, which they had promised to dismantle on numerous occassions.
"I'm worried about tendencies towards creeping secessionism," he said.
Croatian President Franjo Tudjman, patron of the Bosnian Croats, has often been accused of plotting to carve up Bosnia while trying to whitewash Ustasha history.
Diplomats said the Croat mayor of Mostar, Ivan Prskalo, has proposed exhuming bodies of Moslems and Croats buried side by side in a cemetery because of alleged health risks posed by shallow graves.

Diplomats said the proposal appeared to be aimed at creating a separate Croat cemetery which would erase the memory of an alliance between Moslems and Croats at the beginning of the 1992-95 Bosnian war.
"It sounds more like an ethnic cleansing project," said one official.

The Liska cemetery in Croat-controlled western Mostar contains the bodies of Moslems and Croats killed at the beginning of the Bosnian conflict when they fought together as allies against Serb separatists.
A vicious Moslem-Croat war over territory erupted in 1993, leaving the southwestern town of Mostar strictly divided into Moslem and Croat sectors.
When Moslems from eastern Mostar tried to visit the cemetery three months ago, Croat police in uniform and plainclothes beat them and opened fire. One Moslem man was shot dead.
